newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-DAMRON LEADS ST. JUDE CLASSIC IN FIRST ROUND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-DAMRON LEADS ST. JUDE CLASSIC IN FIRST ROUND.

text.p: Robert Damron, one of the most surprising rookies on the PGA Tour, carded a six-under-par 65 and held a one-stroke lead when first-round play was suspended due to darkness at the $1.5 million St. Jude Classic Thursday.
A stroke behind Damron were Nick Price, Craig Kanada and Kenny Perry, who completed their rounds.

Lennie Clements, Doug Martin and Stewart Cink were also at five-under but were on the TPC at Southwind course when play -- which was delayed by thunderstorms for just over three hours -- was suspended at 9:22 p.m.
Seventy-eight of the 155 players were to complete their rounds Friday morning.

Damron, 41st on the money list with $341,758, enjoyed a bogey-free round. The 25-year-old Floridian started on the back nine and ran off five straight pars. He heated up with birdies on 15, 16 and 17.

After parring 18 and the first hole on the front nine, he made birdies at two, three and five to finish at six under. It was the fourth successive round under par for Damron, who tied for third at last week's Buick Classic.
"I carried over confidence from last week," he said. "I changed putters last week and these greens are true."

Price, the 1993 champion here and the only top-20 player entered, is enjoying his best year since 1994, when he won five tour events. He has made the cut in all 10 events he has entered and finished tied for 19th at the U.S. Open two weeks ago. He posted five birdies in a bogey-free round.
Price is competing for the first time since the death of long-time caddie and friend Jeff "Squeeky" Medlen.

Medlen, who was diagnosed with chronic myelogenous leukaemia last summer, died June 16 at the age of 43. He was the caddie during all but one of Price's 14 PGA Tour victories. He helped Price win at the 1992 and 1994 PGA Championships and the 1994 British Open.

South African Ernie Els, coming off successive victories at the U.S. Open and the Buick Classic, is not entered. Also missing are Masters champion Tiger Woods and Jeff Maggert, who finished fourth at the U.S. Open and second to Els at the Buick Classic.
Many top players take time off between the U.S. Open and the British Open in July.

The field does include Greg Norman of Australia, who is making his first appearance since missing the cut at the U.S. Open two weeks ago. Norman, who has played only eight events this year and has missed the cut at both majors, was at three under through 14 holes.

Tied with Norman was defending champion John Cook, who last year set a course record with a 26-under-par 258. He tied the PGA Tour record for best 36-hole total (125) and established a mark for any consecutive 54 holes (189).
The par-71 TPC at Southwind measures 7,006 yards. First prize is $270,000.
